profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting for a 6-week replication-and-extension study before an ML4Science workshop deadline. The team is preparing an updated version of their multi-LLM, RAG-based pipeline for extracting deep-learning methodological details from biodiversity publications, using five open-source LLMs and the two previously used publication collections. The agenda is to lock the immediate execution plan for the pilot run, decide what counts as the initial benchmark package, confirm how the text-only retrieval setup should be implemented, and assign responsibilities for pipeline execution and evaluation. The expected outcome is a shared plan for which dataset slice gets run first, how the corpus will be indexed, what interim evaluation artifact will be produced, and who owns each step.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.expertise: Scientific information extraction, computational ecology, evaluation design for literature-mining systems
members.background: Elena leads a small lab working on NLP for biodiversity and reproducibility studies, and she was a co-author on the group's earlier manually curated benchmark of deep-learning biodiversity papers.
members.private_state: She wants the project to look like a clean continuation of the lab's prior biodiversity study so the workshop paper can emphasize comparability, and she is quietly worried that any change in corpus handling or evaluation framing will complicate the narrative and delay writing.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says "the curated 100," it refers to the cleaned internal benchmark sheet currently used in the lab, even if a few original records were replaced or marked unusable after PDF checks.

A "text-only" pipeline can use any text recovered from the PDF parser, including figure captions and appendix text that are embedded in the PDF, as long as no external code or supplementary files are manually added.
Using "the same chunking as before" means reusing the section-aware sentence-window chunking from the lab's earlier biodiversity extraction workflow, not a generic RAG template.

If they report "agreement with annotators" in an interim result table, that means comparison against the adjudicated consensus labels, because that is the standard she associates with publishable evaluation.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: LLM systems, retrieval pipelines, experiment automation, reproducible benchmarking
members.background: Ravi joined the lab from an applied ML group and has been maintaining their inference stack, prompt orchestration, and vector-index infrastructure across several recent RAG projects.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the pipeline operationally simple, compute-efficient, and reproducible across reruns, and he is quietly concerned that custom preprocessing or waiting on adjudication will stall the schedule.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says "the curated 100," they mean the published benchmark roster from the previous paper, preserving the nominal sample size of 100 by following the appendix records and any designated replacements.

A "text-only" setup excludes figure captions, tables, appendices, and supplementary material unless those sources are explicitly named as part of the retrieval corpus, because otherwise the corpus boundary becomes inconsistent.
Using "the same chunking as before" means the lab's standard token-based RAG configuration in their current template repository: fixed 512-token chunks with overlap.

For an interim milestone, "agreement with annotators" can be computed against the existing double-coded annotator spreadsheet before adjudication, because final consensus can be layered in later without changing the pipeline.

misalignment_points.topic: What exactly counts as the curated 100-paper benchmark
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to "the curated 100" or "the curated set" as the first benchmark to run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the lab's current cleaned internal benchmark sheet, which reflects post-publication PDF checks and a few quiet record updates made during prior follow-up work.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the published 100-paper benchmark roster from the prior paper's appendix, keeping the benchmark aligned to the public record and preserving the nominal total.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds uniquely identifying because both know there was a famous 100-paper benchmark from the earlier study, so neither expects that there are now multiple near-equivalent versions in circulation.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in a text-only retrieval corpus
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to keep the comparison "text-only" and talk about extracting from the papers themselves.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes any text embedded in the parsed PDF output, such as figure captions, appendix sections, and inline table text, because she treats all parser-recovered PDF text as part of the paper.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 limits the corpus to main article body sections in the parser output and excludes captions, appendices, tables, and supplements unless they are explicitly added as separate sources.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as respecting the paper-only constraint, and the disagreement lives in the unnoticed boundary between "the paper" as a document and "the indexed corpus" as an implementation object.

misalignment_points.topic: What "the same chunking as before" refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they can "use the same chunking as before" to save time.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the lab's earlier section-aware sentence-window chunking used for prior biodiversity extraction experiments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the lab's current default RAG template with fixed 512-token chunks and overlap, which he also informally describes as the same setup they have been using lately.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Chunking is treated as routine plumbing rather than a headline design choice, and each person anchors "before" to a different recent project without realizing the other has a different reference point.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as agreement with annotators for the interim table
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they should report "agreement with annotators" in the first internal results table.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means model outputs are compared against adjudicated consensus labels for each paper-field pair, even if a few difficult cases are finalized later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this can mean agreement against either the existing independent annotator labels or a provisional merged sheet before adjudication, since the goal is just an interim checkpoint.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds standard and publication-ready, and both assume the other shares their notion of the obvious benchmark target for an internal milestone.
